device.name: Magic Display
device.notes:
Bluetooth-controlled LED displays for shoes, bags, hats, crafts. Uses Quintic (NXP QN-series) BLE chipset with QPP (Quintic Private Profile) on service 0xFEE9 (chipset is NOT family-wide Quintic: sibling Shining Glasses hardware is Panchip-based with a 0xFD00 OTA service, so Magic Display variants may likewise differ). All command traffic is AES-128-ECB encrypted via the native libAES.so (aes.keyExpansionDefault() is a JNI native method; the 16-byte key is compiled into the .so, NOT present in Java — the recovered key is recorded as static_key on the WRITE1 characteristic below). Commands are fixed 16-byte ASCII-named packets: [length, ASCII_CMD..., params..., zero_pad]. CORRECTION: there is NO connection-time 3-way handshake (the earlier claim was wrong). After connecting, the app simply queries the LED matrix type (STYPE) and parses the response. Bulk image transfer uses DATS (data_transfer_start) framing followed by data frames and DATCP (data_transfer_complete) — that is transfer framing, not an authentication handshake. Supports multiple display sizes: 5x36, 12x48, 14x56, 16x64 (reported via STYPE response). Monochrome 1-bit-per-pixel bitmap encoding (threshold: any RGB channel >= 128 = ON). Device identification by manufacturer-specific adv data: {0x54, 0x52, 0x00, 0x27} ("TR" + 0x0027; ble/BleConfig.java:8, BROADCAST_AiTURE_PRODUCT). No pairing required. Shares the com.cdbwsoft BLE codebase with Shining Glasses. A secondary Texas Instruments profile (service 0xFFF0 / char 0xFFF1) is also supported for TI-based hardware variants. Also has OTA service at 0xFEE8 (Quintic OTA protocol). FEE9/9600 is the generic Quintic-SDK QPP profile reused by unrelated products (e.g. Zhiyun Crane V2 gimbal), so scanning by service UUID alone false-positives — the manufacturer-data prefix match is the real discriminator. CONFIDENCE: command/UUID mapping HIGH (jadx of com.tirohk.magicdisplay); AES key RECOVERED from the arm64 libAES.so bundled in the APK split config.arm64_v8a.apk — 16 bytes at .so file offset 0x3020: 34522a5b7a6e492c08090a9d8d2a23f8, identical to the public iDeal LED family key. App-derived, not yet verified against hardware.
Enrich-branch evidence: version 1.5.6 (versionCode 156) was inspected with jadx. Java class csh.tiro.cc.aes exposes cipher / invCipher / keyExpansion / keyExpansionDefault backed by lib/arm64-v8a/libAES.so; Agreement.getEncryptData() encrypts every command before write and Agreement.getDecodeData() decrypts notifications. Bulk pixel/image upload uses DATS on WRITE1, waits for DATSOK, sends data chunks on WRITE2, then sends DATCP and waits for DATCPOK. CORRECTION (2026-08-14, verified against jadx of com.tirohk.magicdisplay — supersedes the 2026-07-31 sibling-derived notes, which were WRONG for this device): bulk image data on WRITE2 (960a) IS AES-128-ECB encrypted. The app splits the payload into 16-byte blocks ([length][up to 15 payload bytes]), encrypts each block with Agreement.getEncryptData() and writes it with writeCharacteristicBy2 at a fixed 60 ms pacing (data/ImageAgreement.java:404-436; BleDevice.onEncrypt itself is an identity no-op, library/ble/BleDevice.java:130-132). There is NO per-chunk acknowledgement — the string "REOK" appears nowhere in the app; flow control is timing-only. Only the framing commands are acked (DATS→DATSOK, DATCP→DATCPOK). WRITE3 (960b) is likewise encrypted: live DIY writes go through Agreement.getEncryptData() before writeCharacteristicBy3 (activity/LedEditActivity.java:319), and the music/rhythm visualizer sends encrypted 16-byte packets ([0x12][14 bytes of packed 4-bit levels]) on the same channel (music/VisualizerView.java:111-121) — not the sibling's plain 20-byte pixel writes. Multi-frame animation uses a MANY <count> <profile> transaction with per-frame DATS/data/DATCP, closed by MANCPOK (sibling DiyMutiAgreement; unverified for this app). Agreement.parseType maps the STYPE response to a size code: STYPE5X36→536, STYPE5X36N→5360, STYPE12X48→1248, STYPE12X48N→12480, STYPE14X56→1456, STYPE16X64→1664 (data/Agreement.java:44-78; N-suffixed variants exist only for 5X36 and 12X48). Additional observed app features include LIGHTON/LIGHTOFF torch control, MODE 7 music/rhythm mode backed by libint16fft.so, MODE 8/9 connected scroll right/left (daisy-chained displays) with a speed byte (Agreement.java:127-133), SMVEW DIY sync draw, LEDFIRST/LEDSECOND chained display selection, CALL notification passthrough, SCHD/STSC scheduling (timer response prefix "SBHD", Agreement.java:192-208), and ANIM animation selection. Four OTA firmware images are bundled in the app assets: TR1805R03-9_OTA.bin, TR1805R03-10_OTA.bin, TR1806R06-2_OTA.bin, TR1806R06-3_OTA.bin.

credentials.notes: Anything within radio range can connect and issue commands. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state to clear. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the actual remedy for the common failure mode: the device already being connected to another central.

steps.action: Remove power (or battery) for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: No provisioning step: the device advertises as soon as it is powered on and accepts a connection from any central. There is no account, no network credential exchange and no pairing PIN, so a replacement client only has to scan, connect and write.

steps.action: Power the device and scan for its advertisement.
Connect and run the documented initialization sequence, if the spec defines one.

setup.notes: No provisioning. Identify by service UUID and the manufacturer-data prefix rather than by name, since these units advertise without a stable local name.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds this device to a network or an owner, so switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. If the old client is an Android or iOS phone, remove the device from the OS Bluetooth list as well — a cached bond can keep the phone reconnecting automatically and holding the single available link.

data_transfer_start.description: Start bulk data transfer. hi/lo = big-endian 16-bit data length.

multi_frame_animation_start.description: Multi-frame animation transaction: MANY <count> <profile>, then per-frame DATS/data/DATCP; the device closes with MANCPOK (sibling evidence: shining-glasses DiyMutiAgreement). Exact byte layout TBD.

query_device_type.description: Query display dimensions. Response on notify: 'STYPE5X36', 'STYPE12X48', 'STYPE16X64', etc.

characteristics.name: Command (WRITE1)
characteristics.notes: AES-128-ECB, fixed static key. Key recovered verbatim from the vendor APK split's arm64 libAES.so (16 bytes at .so file offset 0x3020); identical to the public iDeal LED family key. The key is compiled into the native lib (loaded via aes.keyExpansionDefault, a JNI method) and is not present in the decompiled Java. App-derived, not yet verified against hardware. Confidence: HIGH structure. Evidence: com/tirohk/magicdisplay/MainApplication.java:26 (keyExpansionDefault); csh/tiro/cc/aes.java:11 (native); com/cdbwsoft/library/ble/BleManager.java:50-57.

characteristics.name: Bulk Data (WRITE2)
characteristics.notes: Bulk image data channel. Data is sent as AES-128-ECB encrypted 16-byte blocks — [length][up to 15 payload bytes] per block, each block passed through Agreement.getEncryptData() before writeCharacteristicBy2, with a fixed 60 ms sleep between blocks (data/ImageAgreement.java:404-436). There is no per-chunk ack ("REOK" appears nowhere in the app); flow control is timing-only. Only the framing commands on WRITE1 are acked (DATS→DATSOK, DATCP→DATCPOK). BleDevice.onEncrypt is an identity no-op (library/ble/BleDevice.java:130-132); the encryption is applied explicitly by the Agreement layer. Verified against jadx of com.tirohk.magicdisplay — supersedes earlier sibling-derived notes claiming unencrypted ~100-byte chunks with REOK flow control.

characteristics.name: Auxiliary (WRITE3)
characteristics.notes: Live DIY pixel writes and music/rhythm visualizer data. Packets are 16-byte and AES-128-ECB encrypted via Agreement.getEncryptData() before writeCharacteristicBy3 (activity/LedEditActivity.java:319); the visualizer sends [0x12][14 bytes of packed 4-bit levels] (music/VisualizerView.java:111-121). Verified against jadx of com.tirohk.magicdisplay — supersedes earlier sibling-derived notes claiming unencrypted 20-byte 05 RR GG BB II packets.

characteristics.name: TI Command
characteristics.notes: TI-variant command characteristic; same AES-128-ECB native key as WRITE1 (recovered from libAES.so, see there). Evidence: BleManager.java:55 (FFF1 characteristic), 58 (FFF0 service).
